doc.title: Charles Lloyd — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Interviewing with Halsey Stevens in 1956
summary: Lloyd interviews at USC with Stevens, who quietly admits the situation is unfair but offers to work with him on the side.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well anyways, so here’s what happened! So to go to SC, in my senior year, they wanted to interview me.

So at Christmastime my mother brought me out to Cali from Memphis. I hadn’t graduated yet - this is deep man, this is ’56 - and I interviewed with Halsey Stevens, cause I wanted to study composition with him.
And he kind of let me know that it was messed up, in a subtle kind of way.
But that he would work with me on the side.
That’s heavy. Cause I was curious to know if he was an ally or not.
Wait a minute. I’m just telling you he’d work with me on the side, cause what I had wasn’t presentable in their way. But he knew that I knew harmony and stuff.
Cause I knew changes, and I knew how to modulate, and I knew substitutions and I knew stuff, cause Phineas - he showed me a bunch of stuff!
